case_title: Asim Shariff v. National Investigation Agency
evidence_type: Charge-sheet material: mobile/telephone call records, seized banner, disclosure report, bank and call data; no direct eyewitness evidence against the accused discussed
confession: Alleged confession by co-accused no. 4 naming the accused as mastermind (prosecution allegation; not relied on by the Court). Defence counsel admitted PFI membership and frequent phone conversations before the trial court, which the trial court relied on.
aggravating_circumstances: Prosecution alleged the act was intended to create fear and insecurity among people at large; not noted as aggravating by the Court
trial_court_outcome: Section 227 CrPC discharge application dismissed; charges framed against the accused for all offences in the charge sheet (order dated 2 January 2018; a later passage refers to 12 January 2018)
high_court_outcome: Writ petition under Articles 226 and 227 and s.482 CrPC dismissed; trial court order affirmed
neutral_facts: On 16 October 2016 at about 12.40 p.m., a group of friends of the victim had assembled near a medical store in Shivajinagar when a person riding pillion on a motorcycle struck the victim on the right side of the neck with a sharp-edged machete and fled. The victim was taken to hospital and declared brought dead. A companion who was present lodged a complaint, and the police registered a murder case. Four persons were arrested within about eleven days, and a fifth shortly afterwards. The investigation was then transferred to the National Investigation Agency, which filed a charge sheet against all five. The prosecution alleged that the accused had conspired to kill members of an opposing organisation and that the killing was a planned act meant to create fear among a section of people. Evidence relied on included mobile phone call records between the accused, bank account details, a seized banner bearing photographs of the accused, and a disclosure report describing a leather purse containing a letter listing earlier killings. It was further alleged that the accused had attended indoctrination classes and that one co-accused had confessed that this accused was the mastermind. Several witnesses who attended search and seizure proceedings gave information on bank and call data. The defence contended that no incriminating material had been recovered against the accused.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a single machete blow to the neck (throat slit)
number_of_offences: 13 charged (IPC ss.120B, 109, 150, 153A, 302, 201; Arms Act ss.3, 27; UAP Act ss.15, 16, 17, 18, 20); 0 finally upheld as convictions (no trial conclusion; discharge refused)
premeditation_planning: Court found only prima facie material of conspiracy among the accused, to be examined at trial; planning was alleged by the prosecution, not decided
motive: alleged: conspiracy to kill members of an organisation and to strike terror among a section of people
key_evidence_accepted: Charge-sheet material showing frequent telephone/mobile conversations between the accused, together with defence counsel's admissions on organisational roles and calls (assessed only for prima facie purposes)
witness_credibility: Not assessed; the Court did not evaluate witness credibility at the discharge stage
custody_duration: Arrested 2 November 2016; total duration of custody not stated
trial_duration: offence: 16 October 2016; trial judgment: 2 January 2018 (order dismissing discharge; another passage gives 12 January 2018); High Court: 22 November 2018; Supreme Court: 1 July 2019
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): Kamini Jaiswal, Abdul Rahiman, Shereef K.A., Ms. Rani Mishra, Jatinderpal Singh (Advocates). State/respondent (NIA): Aman Lekhi, ASG, with Ms. Shraddha Deshmukh, Kanu Agrawal, B. V. Balaram Das (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No. 124/2016, then NIA RC No. 24/2016); investigation transferred to NIA; charge sheet filed 21 April 2017; charges framed; trial pending
appeal_history: Trial court: discharge dismissed and charges framed. High Court: writ petition dismissed, order affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Section 15 UAP Act covers individual and gang acts and Section 20 does not require the organisation to be scheduled; the act was intended to create fear; series of evidence (calls, banner, disclosure report, indoctrination classes, co-accused's alleged confession) shows involvement
defence_argument: No material linking the accused to the offence; charge based on suspicion; nothing incriminating recovered; the Navaratri/Vijayadashmi dating in the prosecution story was wrong; UAP Act not attracted as no accused belonged to a banned organisation; CW witnesses gave nothing against the accused
legal_principle_applied: Under s.227 CrPC the judge may sift and weigh evidence only to find whether a prima facie case exists; grave suspicion justifies framing charge; if two views are possible and one gives only suspicion, discharge may follow; no mini trial
precedent_relied_upon: Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal (1979) 3 SCC 4; Sajjan Kumar v. Central Bureau of Investigation (2010) 9 SCC 368; State v. S. Selvi (2018) 13 SCC 455; Vikram Johar v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2019) 6 SCALE 794
